projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The stable presence count of 25-27 devices at 3 AM, combined with zero camera activity and Roxanne’s normal sleep metrics, confirms the household is securely asleep and the high device count is likely an IoT baseline artifact rather than human movement.

The stable device count (23–27) paired with zero camera motion at 11:24 PM confirms a normal nighttime state where personal electronics and IoT devices are stationary and charging, indicating the earlier flags are likely false positives from standard device tracking rather than an unusual event.

The sustained presence of 23–26 mobile devices paired with zero camera motion for four hours strongly suggests either a large group of quiet guests (like a sleepover or family visit) or a network tracking artifact, warranting a quick verification to ensure everyone is safe and accounted for.

The sustained presence of 23–26 mobile devices paired with zero camera motion over four hours strongly suggests either unaccounted stationary guests/devices in the home or a network configuration error misclassifying IoT gadgets as phones, warranting verification to rule out unauthorized access or sensor drift.

The sustained 22-26 device count vastly exceeds the household size, and paired with zero camera motion for four hours, strongly indicates a stationary gathering or IoT network surge rather than active presence, warranting verification to rule out unauthorized access or sensor misconfiguration.

The sustained 22-26 'mobile' device count paired with zero camera motion for four hours strongly suggests a network misclassification of stationary IoT devices as mobile, or the household is in a highly contained, quiet state. This warrants a quick network check to ensure presence tracking accuracy and rule out camera blind spots or reporting errors.

The sustained 22-26 device count on a weekday afternoon, paired with zero camera motion, strongly indicates either IoT gadgets being miscounted as mobile devices or unaccounted guests on the network, warranting a quick verification to rule out unauthorized access.

The sustained high device count paired with zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon strongly indicates a network misclassification of IoT devices rather than actual occupancy, suggesting no security concern despite the earlier medium alerts.

The sustained 20–24 device count paired with zero camera motion strongly indicates a network presence detection anomaly (likely phantom IoT connections or guest network bleed) rather than actual occupancy, as the four-person household would generate motion; this warrants a network check to prevent false automations.

The sustained 20–23 device count paired with zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon strongly suggests either a large gathering in camera-blind zones or a network/IoT counting anomaly. This warrants a quick verification to rule out unauthorized access or misreported presence.
